metadata.description: AI Infrastructure Unwinding Monitor - June 2026 refresh. Q1 2026 earnings cycle: hyperscaler capex still rising (~$700-725B combined 2026 guidance), cloud + semiconductor revenue accelerating, but FCF collapsing and the first broad AI-infrastructure equity selloff (Jun 5-6, 2026). Added TSMC, AMD, Broadcom, Super Micro, Vertiv per data/companies.json.

risk_rationale.summary: Composite Risk Score of 7/40 holds at LOW. Through the Q1 2026 earnings cycle the LAGGING operating fundamentals remain strong: all four hyperscalers RAISED 2026 capex guidance (no cuts), cloud revenue accelerated (AWS +28%, Google Cloud +63%, Azure ~40%), and semiconductor demand re-accelerated (NVIDIA Data Center +92% YoY, Broadcom AI +143%). No capex reductions means we remain in Pre-Phase 1. However the risk has migrated beneath the top line and into the LEADING layer (see leading file, composite 5->12).
risk_rationale.why_low: No Phase 1 trigger: zero capex cuts, zero project cancellations, AI/cloud revenue accelerating, chip orders accelerating. The score stays at 7 rather than falling because the quality of growth is deteriorating even as the rate improves.
risk_rationale.concerns: The 7 points reflect: AI revenue growth quality (AWS/Azure in the 20-40% band = YELLOW even as GCP accelerates), margin/FCF compression (operating margins stable but TTM free cash flow collapsed - Amazon ~$38B->$1.2B, Alphabet -38%, Microsoft -22% - on a depreciation ramp; Michael Burry argued the group understates depreciation ~$176B over 2026-28), weak enterprise ROI proof (~29% report significant GenAI ROI, Deloitte 2026), and unproven inference cost economics.
risk_rationale.key_watch: Power has become the binding constraint (DOE emergency curtailment order May 2026; PJM watchdog asked FERC to halt new data-center interconnections). The first broad AI-infrastructure equity selloff hit Jun 5-6, 2026 (Nasdaq -4.2%, ~$1.71T in a day, triggered by Broadcom guidance). Watch Q2 2026 earnings (late Jul/Aug) for the first capex-guidance moderation - none yet. Oracle and CoreWeave are where financing stress is sharpest.

indicator_scoring.formula: Composite Risk Score = Sum (Indicator Points x Multiplier)

indicators.name: Capex Guidance
indicators.description: All four hyperscalers RAISED 2026 capex guidance in Q4 2025/Q1 2026; combined ~$700-725B. No cuts.

indicators.name: AI Revenue Growth
indicators.description: Mixed: Google Cloud +63% and Azure ~40% strong, but AWS +28% sits in the 20-40% band and FCF shows monetization lagging spend.

indicators.name: GPU Utilization
indicators.description: GPUs sold out; secondary rental prices rose ~40% on a renewed shortage. No excess capacity.

indicators.name: Margin Compression
indicators.description: Operating margins stable/expanding, but TTM free cash flow collapsed across hyperscalers as depreciation ramps.

indicators.name: Timeline Changes
indicators.description: No project delays or cancellations. Power constraints emerging as a buildout risk but no announced pauses yet.

indicators.name: Enterprise Adoption
indicators.description: ROI proof still weak - only ~29% report significant GenAI ROI; 79% cite adoption challenges (Deloitte 2026).

indicators.name: Cost Economics
indicators.description: Inference costs keep falling (growth-positive) but are partly subsidy-supported; durable unit economics unproven.

indicators.name: Semiconductor Orders
indicators.description: Re-accelerating: NVIDIA Data Center +92% YoY, Broadcom AI semi +143%, TSMC raised capex. No cancellations.

active_signals.title: AI-Bubble Selloff: Nasdaq Sheds ~$1.71T in a Single Day
active_signals.description: On June 5-6, 2026 a broad AI-infrastructure equity selloff hit markets (Nasdaq -4.2%, ~$1.71 trillion erased in one day, NVDA -6%), triggered by underwhelming Broadcom guidance. The first major correlated repricing of the AI-infra complex - the kind of single-catalyst, whole-group drawdown the correlation indicator exists to catch.

active_signals.title: Oracle Financing Stress: Negative FCF, Moody's Cut, Bondholder Lawsuit
active_signals.description: Oracle FY2026 free cash flow ran ~-$24.7B TTM against >$100B debt; Moody's moved its outlook to negative; and a January 2026 bondholder lawsuit alleges the $18B Sept-2025 offering concealed the scale of further debt needed for the $300B OpenAI/Stargate buildout. The clearest single-name credit escalation in this monitor.

active_signals.title: Hyperscaler Free Cash Flow Collapses Beneath Strong Top Line
active_signals.description: Despite raised capex and accelerating cloud revenue, TTM free cash flow collapsed (Amazon ~$38B -> ~$1.2B, Alphabet -38%, Microsoft -22%) as short-lived GPU assets drive a depreciation ramp. Michael Burry publicly argued the group understates depreciation by ~$176B over 2026-28.

active_signals.title: Power Becomes the Binding Constraint on AI Buildout
active_signals.description: The DOE issued an emergency order (May 2026) allowing PJM to curtail data centers, and PJM's market monitor asked FERC to halt new data-center interconnections amid a ~2,600 GW queue and record capacity prices. Power, not GPUs, now gates the next order-of-magnitude of training compute.

active_signals.title: Capex Still Rising: All Four Hyperscalers Raised 2026 Guidance
active_signals.description: No moderation through Q1 2026: combined 2026 capex guidance reached ~$700-725B (Amazon ~$200B, Alphabet $180-190B, Microsoft ~$145B annualized, Meta $125-145B), with Alphabet and Meta raising mid-cycle. Cloud growth accelerated (AWS +28%, Google Cloud +63%). A clearly positive demand signal.

active_signals.title: Semiconductor Demand Re-Accelerating
active_signals.description: NVIDIA Data Center revenue +92% YoY (Q1 FY2027, $75.2B), Broadcom AI semiconductor +143% YoY (guide >+200% next quarter), AMD Data Center +57%, and TSMC raised 2026 capex to $52-56B on AI/HPC demand. No order cancellations or demand softening anywhere in the chain.

companies.name: Microsoft (MSFT)
companies.capex: ~$145B annualized FY2026 (Q3 FY26: $30.9B, +84% YoY) - still rising
companies.ai_growth: Azure +40% YoY; AI run-rate $37B (+123% YoY); RPO $625B
companies.margin: Stable; FCF -22% YoY on depreciation ramp
companies.notes: Azure still supply-constrained at +40% with a $625B (OpenAI-heavy) backlog. Only flag is the FCF/depreciation compression, not demand.

companies.name: Amazon (AMZN)
companies.margin: Record 13.1% op margin; TTM FCF collapsed to ~$1.2B
companies.notes: AWS reaccelerated to +28% and margins expanded, but near-zero free cash flow on a $200B capex plan is the watch item.

companies.name: Alphabet (GOOGL)
companies.notes: Strongest cloud growth of the four (+63%) with a near-doubled backlog; offset by the steepest FCF decline.

companies.name: Meta (META)
companies.ai_growth: No direct AI revenue; AI lifted ad conversions >6%
companies.notes: Raised capex again and stock fell ~7% on the raise despite a revenue beat - the clearest ongoing investor-ROI-skepticism signal among the four.

companies.name: NVIDIA (NVDA)
companies.ai_growth: Data Center $75.2B Q1 FY2027 (+92% YoY) - re-accelerating
companies.notes: Blackwell at full scale, Vera Rubin ramping; no demand softening. Raised dividend and added an $80B buyback.

companies.name: TSMC (TSM)
companies.ai_growth: Q1 2026 $35.9B (+35% YoY); HPC 61% of mix; FY guide >30%
companies.notes: AI/HPC demand and capex both raised. One nuance: April monthly revenue +17.5% YoY was the slowest in ~6 months - a single deceleration datapoint to watch.

companies.name: AMD (AMD)
companies.ai_growth: Data Center $5.8B Q1 2026 (+57% YoY); MI450 Meta win
companies.notes: CEO called AI demand 'sky high'; MI350 shipping and an MI450 1GW Meta deployment de-risks the 2026-27 ramp. Smaller scale than NVDA.

companies.name: Broadcom (AVGO)
companies.ai_growth: AI semi $10.8B Q2 FY26 (+143% YoY); Q3 guide >+200%
companies.notes: Custom-silicon + networking accelerating across six accelerator customers (incl. Google, Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic); reiterated >$100B AI revenue for FY2027. (Its soft total-revenue guide triggered the Jun 6 selloff.)

companies.name: Oracle (ORCL)
companies.notes: Backlog enormous but financing stress intensifying: Moody's negative outlook and a Jan 2026 bondholder lawsuit over $18B-offering disclosures tied to the $300B OpenAI/Stargate deal. Clearest single-name escalation.

companies.name: CoreWeave (CRWV)
companies.capex: Raised; >1 GW active / 3.5 GW contracted power
companies.margin: Net loss $740M; interest expense doubled to $536M
companies.notes: Growth decelerated from 355% but base is larger; top-customer concentration improved ~67%->45%. Raised an $8.5B HPC-backed debt facility; CDS distressed (~600-770bps). The credit canary.

companies.name: Nebius (NBIS)
companies.notes: Best growth profile in the group; signed a $27B/5yr Meta deal and 1.2 GW in Pennsylvania. Risk nudges up on the capex ramp ($20-25B vs ~$3B revenue) funded via converts/warrants.

companies.name: Iris Energy (IREN)
companies.notes: Signed a $3.4B AI-cloud / 5 GW NVIDIA partnership. Total revenue fell QoQ and legacy mining is shrinking faster than AI fills in - a transitional-stress signal.

companies.name: Applied Digital (APLD)
companies.capex: 600 MW under contract; Polaris Forge 1 live
companies.notes: Revenue beat as lease revenue became the primary driver, but heavy single-counterparty dependence on CoreWeave is a direct transmission channel for CRWV's stress.

companies.name: Dell Technologies (DELL)
companies.ai_growth: $24.4B AI orders Q1 FY27; $16.1B AI-server rev; FY27 guide $60B
companies.notes: Demand accelerated, not decelerated - stock had its best day ever (+32%). $43B AI backlog. A clean demand barometer flashing strong, no financing/accounting stress.

companies.name: Super Micro (SMCI)
companies.ai_growth: Q2 FY2026 $12.7B (+123% YoY); FY26 guide raised to >=$40B
companies.notes: Explosive revenue but thin, working-capital-intensive margins on the DLC ramp. Accounting/governance overhang eased (BDO audit, no restatement) but some institutional skepticism persists.

companies.name: Vertiv (VRT)
companies.notes: Cleanest 'is demand still there?' proxy and strongly affirmative - book-to-bill >1, ~80%+ backlog growth, raised guidance. Power/cooling remains a genuine bottleneck.

capex_guidance.notes: All four hyperscalers raised 2026 capex guidance; combined ~$700-725B. No moderation through Q1 2026.

ai_revenue_growth.notes: Google Cloud +63% and Azure ~40% strong; AWS +28% in the 20-40% band. FCF collapse signals monetization lagging spend.

gpu_utilization.notes: GPUs sold out; secondary rental prices reversed upward ~40% on a renewed shortage. No excess capacity.

margin_compression.notes: Operating margins stable/expanding but TTM free cash flow collapsed on a depreciation ramp. Burry flagged ~$176B understated depreciation 2026-28.

timeline_changes.notes: No project pauses, but power has become the binding constraint (DOE emergency curtailment; FERC interconnection-halt request).

semiconductor_orders.notes: NVIDIA DC +92% YoY, Broadcom AI +143% (guide >+200%), AMD DC +57%, TSMC raised capex. No cancellations.

credit_spreads.notes: Investment-grade hyperscaler credit fine, but CoreWeave CDS distressed (~600-770bps) and Oracle on Moody's negative outlook + bondholder lawsuit.

private_valuations.notes: OpenAI $852B, Anthropic ~$965B, xAI ~$230B. Record funding but ~65% of all Q1 VC in 3-4 labs; IPO-exit rush and tail down-rounds.

quarterly_updates.summary: Q1 2026 earnings confirmed continued capex escalation and accelerating cloud + semiconductor revenue, but with deteriorating quality (FCF collapse, depreciation drag) and a first broad AI-infrastructure equity selloff on Jun 5-6. Added TSMC, AMD, Broadcom, Super Micro, and Vertiv to the tracked roster. Lagging composite holds at 7/40 (LOW, Pre-Phase 1); the leading layer doubled to 12/48.
highlights: All four hyperscalers RAISED 2026 capex; combined ~$700-725B guidance - no moderation
Cloud accelerated: AWS +28%, Google Cloud +63%, Azure ~40%; Microsoft AI run-rate $37B (+123%)
Semis re-accelerated: NVIDIA DC +92% YoY, Broadcom AI +143%, AMD DC +57%, TSMC capex raised to $52-56B
But TTM free cash flow collapsed (Amazon ~$38B->$1.2B, Alphabet -38%, Microsoft -22%) on depreciation ramp
Jun 5-6 2026: broad AI-infra selloff, Nasdaq -4.2%, ~$1.71T erased in a day (Broadcom-guidance trigger)
Oracle financing stress: Moody's negative outlook + bondholder lawsuit; CoreWeave CDS distressed
Power became the binding constraint: DOE emergency curtailment order; FERC interconnection-halt request

quarterly_updates.summary: Hyperscaler capex acceleration continued; NVIDIA Q3 crushed estimates; Dell added with record AI server orders. Meta market reaction signaled emerging investor skepticism. Risk LOW at 7/40.
highlights: NVIDIA Q3 FY2026: $57.01B revenue (+62.5% YoY), Data Center $51.2B (+66% YoY)
Dell record $12.3B AI server orders (Q3), $18.4B backlog
All hyperscalers raised 2025 capex guidance; collective >$380B
Meta stock dropped 11% despite a beat - first ROI-skepticism signal

top_warnings: AI-infrastructure equity selloff (~$1.71T in a day, Jun 6)
Broadcom guidance disappointment triggers broad repricing
CoreWeave credit-default-swap spreads in distressed territory

phases_section.heading: 📊 Unwinding Phases
phases_section.intro: Six-phase model tracking AI infrastructure unwinding from initial capex reductions to market reset.

lagging_popover.description: Composite risk score from quarterly earnings reports. Tracks capex guidance, AI revenue growth, utilization rates, operating margins, and other Phase 1 indicators that confirm unwinding after it has begun.

phase_popover.description: Current phase in the 6-phase unwinding model. Pre-Phase 1 means no unwinding signals detected. Phase 1 would indicate capex guidance reductions by hyperscalers.

signals_popover.description: Number of active signals being tracked. Positive signals (severity: low) indicate healthy developments like capex increases or earnings beats. Negative signals (severity: moderate/high) indicate concerns like investor skepticism or guidance misses.
